reasons: Claimed status is 'compliant' with no redline and no comment, which is the expected output shape; the rendered redline is identical to the original paragraph, so nothing invalid or directionally wrong has been introduced.

The cited text supports the classification: paragraph 4(a) gives Customer a for-any-reason termination right on 90 days' written notice following the Initial Term, which sits at the outer edge of the 60–90 day fallback window.

The missing-behaviour test is correctly not triggered: the Initial Term is a single 12 months (auto-renewing in 1-year increments), not a term 'longer than 12 months', so the absence of an in-term convenience right is not a deviation under the detection guidance.

Vendor's mirrored right carries a full 90 days' notice and cannot be exercised during the Initial Term, so it does not reach the walk-away trigger (Vendor convenience on fewer than 90 days). The rationale candidly flags that 'following the Initial Term' is slightly broader than the fallback's 'end of a term' phrasing and treats it as a noted sub-element rather than a deviation — a defensible call given the symmetry benefits us.

Kubient's entitlement to 'all fees generated during the termination period' is fees earned during the notice window rather than an early-termination penalty, and in any event falls below the fallback's 3-months'-fees ceiling.

The failed deterministic check ('Customer convenience termination present') is explained as a phrasing artifact of the bilateral 'Either Party may terminate' construction, which is accurate on the face of the text.
Minor shortfalls versus the preferred position (no express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; no partial/Exhibit-level termination) are correctly noted in the rationale rather than redlined.
